title: Orientation, Setup & Your Learning Path
authority: Placement recommendations preserve all existing content. They do not alter the canonical curriculum until separately approved and committed.

items.title: By the end of this module
items.reason: Replace broad orientation language with observable outcomes tied to the Learning Charter.

items.title: How this course works
items.reason: Every learner needs the shared curriculum, role-lens, evidence, assessment, and support model.

items.title: Getting set up
items.reason: Keep universal access, account, browser, support, accessibility, and approved storage setup. Route specialized technical setup elsewhere.

items.title: The placement diagnostic
items.reason: Convert the diagnostic into a support-routing baseline with no employment, aptitude, or credential use.

items.title: The rules of the road
items.reason: Teach source, privacy, evidence, attribution, human-authority, and participation rules through realistic classification.

items.title: Role takeaways
items.reason: Connect each role to decisions and cross-role relationships without creating separate curricula.

items.title: Glossary
items.reason: Keep only terms used in M00 and define them in plain English before glossary review.

items.title: Now you're ready
items.reason: Replace a generic closing with the saved Learning Charter, first accountable action, and transition to M01.

items.title: Sources
items.reason: Preserve source, limitation, permission, and internal-program-decision boundaries.

items.title: The terminal, from zero
items.reason: Terminal fluency supports builders but is not a universal Academy entry outcome. Preserve it as Builder Readiness preparation and teach it in depth where building begins.

items.title: API keys and the .env file: where your secrets live
items.reason: M00 needs a plain safety preview. Security and hands-on use belong with cybersecurity and building instruction.

items.title: Your code editor: install Cursor or VS Code, and read code you didn't write
items.reason: Code-editor setup is relevant to the build sequence, not every learner's orientation.

items.title: Get an API key without a surprise bill
items.reason: Preserve the duplicate ID and history while managing one coherent secrets, cost-control, and key-safety proposal.

items.title: Environment variables and secrets
items.reason: Preserve Shreya's reinforcement and route detailed practice to security and building contexts.

items.title: JSON, YAML, CSV, and Markdown
items.reason: Use a light diagnostic in M00. Teach identification, editing, and validation where data and reusable instructions require these formats.

items.title: Command line and terminal
items.reason: Preserve the source contribution and attach it to the Builder Readiness and M40 placement decision.
